reasons: The claimed missing-behaviour deviation is supported: Section 11.1 commits Corio to a five-year initial term with automatic renewals, and Section 11.2 permits termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency, so there is no Customer convenience exit in a term longer than 12 months.

The inserted Section 11.4 hits the preferred position squarely: Customer (Corio) convenience termination in whole or in part on 30 days' written notice, no early-termination fee or penalty, pro-rata refund of prepaid license/support/maintenance fees, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during the initial or renewal term.

The edit is additive and minimal — existing 11.1/11.2/11.3 language is left intact and the new subsection is placed logically after 11.3, so the high changed-character footprint is purely the new clause rather than a rewrite.

The failed 'Customer convenience termination present' check is a naming variant only: the clause uses the actual party name 'Corio' (the customer) rather than the literal token 'Customer', so substance satisfies the rule.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, explains the change, and offers the 60-day fallback without lecturing.
